stories.title: Before Megaspeed, there was Supermicro: The other Nvidia partner tied to China chip smuggling—and to Jensen Huang
stories.summary: Prosecutors are now reportedly probing whether Alice Huang and entities linked to her helped move Supermicro hardware to China—and authorities in Singapore say Supermicro hasn’t been forthcoming.

sources.name: Fortune
sources.title: Before Megaspeed, there was Supermicro: The other Nvidia partner tied to China chip smuggling—and to Jensen Huang
sources.text: Whether she was a spy, a fixer, or just a paramour of Jensen Huang, the name Alice Huang (no relation) has roiled the business world this week following reports that the two were having an affair. The revelation snowballed into Jensen’s shocking resignation Wednesday. Now come reports that officials are looking into other companies Alice was working with. Bloomberg reported , based on an anonymous source, that the Department of Justice is running multiple probes into Nvidia . One is focused on antitrust issues and two others are focused on Megaspeed—where Alice Huang was a former top executive—and Super Micro Computer . Separately, the U.S. Attorney’s Office in Manhattan is probing whether entities linked to Alice Huang were involved in alleged efforts to smuggle Supermicro hardware laced with Nvidia’s red-hot GPUs into China. It is unclear whether that probe is tied to smuggling cases already brought in the U.S. or Asia. Neither Jensen Huang, Nvidia, nor Supermicro have been formally charged with any wrongdoing. Supermicro stock tumbled 12% after U.S. markets opened this morning. The company did not immediately respond to Fortune ’s request for comment. Thus far, much of the speculation about Jensen Huang’s catastrophic downfall as the leader of Nvidia has centered on Megaspeed, the Singapore firm that reportedly became one of Nvidia’s largest buyers in Southeast Asia. But Supermicro, the San Jose server maker run by Charles Liang, Jensen Huang’s friend of three decades and an important partner to Nvidia, has been in under the microscope regarding export-control compliance and is being pulled along with Nvidia. Fortune has reported on the Supermicro case since before federal agents arrested its co-founder in March, and that reporting shows a company with a documented track record of governance and compliance failures. Despite its history, Supermicro has remained in lockstep with Nvidia. Liang and Jensen have shared the stage together at Computex in Taiwan, where Jensen was photographed in 2024 with Alice at a cocktail bar. In March, federal prosecutors charged Supermicro co-founder Yih-Shyan “Wally” Liaw and two others with allegedly routing about $2.5 billion in servers laced with Nvidia H200 and B200 GPUs to China through a Southeast Asian front company. Bloomberg later reported the front company is OBON, a Bangkok-based AI infrastructure firm, which has not been charged. Supermicro was not charged and has said it was a victim of the scheme. Liaw, who immediately resigned his executive and board roles at Supermicro following his arrest, has pleaded not guilty. His trial was pushed to March 2027 after Liaw’s lawyers told the judge in his case that subpoenas issued to Supermicro could be material to Liaw’s defense. Nelson Boxer, Liaw’s attorney, declined to comment. One of Liaw’s co-defendants in the smuggling case, Ting-Wei “Willy” Sun, pleaded guilty in October, including to a charge that he deleted an encrypted messaging app from his phone on the day of the arrests. Sun’s attorneys did not respond to a request for comment, and it’s unclear if Sun has a cooperation agreement with the government. There is no public evidence so far that the Supermicro and Megaspeed cases are directly connected but there are mounting threads. Thursday, Singapore’s Ministry of Home Affairs issued a statement noting that the Singapore Police Force and Customs had initiated investigations into Megaspeed and Alice Huang and in doing so sought information from Supermicro. Supermicro only offered “limited cooperation,” Singaporean authorities said. In a July 2025 meeting, Singapore officials raised this with U.S. authorities and asked for their assistance in getting Supermicro’s cooperation and have repeated the request “on several occasions” to the Department of Justice and the FBI. “Despite these repeated requests, Singapore has to date received limited information or assistance in respect of the company,” the statement reads. In a statement to Fortune, a Supermicro spokesperson said it “has been responsive to inquiries and fully cooperated with U.S. and Taiwanese officials, while also voluntarily providing information and engaging with all requests from Singapore authorities to date.” The company added that “Megaspeed is not, and has never been, a Supermicro customer.” Supermicro’s export-control problems did not start with Liaw’s arrest, Fortune ’s reporting has found. In 2006, the company pleaded guilty to illegally exporting computer equipment to Iran through a distributor in Dubai, mirroring the basic scheme prosecutors alleged in the Liaw case. Liaw himself has been through the crisis wringer before. He left Supermicro in 2018 amid a board-led investigation tied to Supermicro’s Nasdaq delisting and an SEC probe of its accounting, which ended with a $17.5 million settlement in 2020. Liaw returned as a consultant in May 2021, became a full-time employee, and rejoined the board in December 2023. In 2024, short seller Hindenburg Research accused Supermicro of accounting manipulation and export-control failures and the company denied the allegations. Ernst & Young then resigned as auditor mid-audit, saying it could no longer rely on management’s representations. A special committee recommended in December 2024 that Supermicro replace CFO David Weigand and the company agreed to do so “immediately .” The company didn’t name a successor until October. As Fortune has reported, the Liaw indictment describes thousands of nonworking dummy servers staged in warehouses to fool auditors, contractors using hair dryers to peel off serial-number labels, and a compliance auditor who was off-site allegedly enjoying “entertainment” paid for by another company during an inspection. It also shows how the alleged scheme fed directly into Nvidia’s supply pipeline. sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Alice Huang tied to Nvidia’s biggest Chinese competitor
sources.text: Alleged Chinese spy Alice Huang may have owned stakes in businesses in China that benefited Nvidia's biggest competitor in China, Huawei, at the same time that she was in business with Nvidia and also reportedly having a romantic affair with its ousted CEO Jensen Huang . The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei was first discovered by analysts at private intelligence firm Tesari. The firm exclusively shared its findings with CNBC. Tesari, which uses artificial intelligence to collect evidence and specializes in national security investigations around the world, provides intelligence research to private companies and the U.S. government. This previously unreported entanglement may raise questions about Alice Huang's intent and conduct in her relationship with the CEO and whether Jensen Huang knew his romantic partner was closely connected with his competition. Jensen Huang has acknowledged having an affair, though the precise timing of his relationship with Alice Huang is unknown. The mysterious saga of Alice Huang involves a tangle of interlocking corporations and transactions that show her connection to entities that ultimately provided computing power to Huawei in China. Huawei is known as a Chinese government "state champion" in the technology and telecommunications sectors, meaning it receives enormous financial support from the government in Beijing so it can lower prices and undercut global competitors. It is considered a key part of the Chinese government's push for global technical dominance and is closely linked to the Chinese Communist Party. Businesses connected to Alice Huang were linked with supplying Nvidia computing power to Huawei, according to documents reviewed by CNBC, around the same time she and Jensen Huang were first publicly seen together, in December 2023. In 2024, Nvidia said Huawei was a top competitor , specifically in artificial intelligence chips including graphics processing units, central processing units and networking chips. "This activity, which surfaced through our analysis of Alice's network, warrants a national security and [technology] counterproliferation investigation," said Brian Andersen, Tesari's vice president for national security applications and a former supervisory special agent with Homeland Security Investigations. If the Commerce Department's Bureau of Industry Security and Homeland Security Investigations found evidence that anyone transferred "controlled equipment" to Huawei without authorization, potential charges might include export-control violations, conspiracy and smuggling, Andersen said. The connection between Alice Huang and Huawei is so convoluted that analysts at Tesari told CNBC that based on their previous investigative experience, they suspect it was designed to deliberately obscure the relationship. Nvidia and Huawei did not respond to CNBC's requests for comment. Jensen Huang did not respond to a voicemail left on a mobile phone. Alice Huang could not be reached. According to Chinese corporate records and media reports compiled by Tesari and provided to CNBC, Alice Huang, whose Chinese name is Huang Le and who according to documents at the time was based in Hong Kong, in 2019 sold a cloud business she owned called Osmanthus to a Chinese gaming company called 7Road. A subsidiary of 7Road, which was based in Singapore, was spun off as "Megaspeed" in 2023 . Megaspeed would go on to become a key Nvidia customer, helping facilitate at least $7.5 billion in Nvidia chip shipments to Chinese firms, The Information reported Tuesday. As early as 2016, Alice Huang had also become a co-owner of a financial firm known as Shanghai Hexi , which heavily invests in tech and data centers. In 2021, Hexi in turn acquired 27 percent of a company called Shanghai Century Longteng, a data center developer, which Hexi held until 2024 . That firm owned a controlling 50.1 percent stake in a data center facility called Shenzhen Yifeng Technology Co. Ltd. in mainland China. The key customer of that data center was Huawei Cloud , the Shenzhen, China-based subsidiary of Huawei Technologies. In addition, Alice Huang's firm Hexi guaranteed the loans required to finance the Shenzhen data center, which did business with Huawei. Hexi did not immediately respond to a message via its LinkedIn page sent outside of normal business hours. CNBC translated corporate records and Chinese news articles in Mandarin that Tesari provided. It's not clear if the Shenzhen data center was able to acquire Nvidia GPUs, but its majority owner began purchasing the chips in 2023 . That company is known as Zhejiang Century Huatong Group and is a business partner of Alice Huang's Hexi through their joint ownership of Century Longteng. That made Alice Huang a part owner of a data center providing computing power to Huawei. And that was happening at around the same time the first known sightings of Alice Huang and Jensen Huang in public together. And that raises the question of why Huawei, which has access to Chinese-made chips, would need to rent computing power from an outside entity. Hexi exited its stake in the data center development company in 2024, but individuals within Alice Huang's network are still connected to the Shenzhen data center. Her husband Kang Wei is a longtime business associate who founded Hexi, where Alice Huang previously held an executive role. In 2022, Kang became an executive of Century Longteng, which owns the controlling stake in the Shenzhen data center, and he also attended the company's signing of the Huawei agreement.

sources.name: Engadget
sources.title: Bloomberg details web of Chinese AI companies with smuggled NVIDIA chips linked to Alice Huang
sources.text: The NVIDIA chips involved are banned in China. A Chinese company with ties to Alice Huang procured NVIDIA AI chips banned in the country, which were then installed at a Shanghai AI facility that also has ties to Alice Huang, according to Bloomberg . The publication says the documents it has reviewed for its report shows explicit evidence that there's a network of Chinese companies, which have managed to get their hands on NVIDIA chips that weren't supposed to be sold in China, with Huang at the center. US officials believe that Alice Huang is a spy recruited by China's main intelligence agency to target NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang. The goal was apparently to learn more about America's AI plans and to get Jensen Huang to persuade the US government to let his company ship its more advanced chips to China. Before he stepped down as CEO of NVIDIA , Jensen Huang reportedly admitted in a staff memo that he had an affair with Alice Huang. To the public, Alice was an executive at Singaporean company Megaspeed, but the reports that had come out since the issue blew up paint a different picture of who she truly was. Bloomberg says the NVIDIA chips listed in the documents it reviewed were sold to Aperia Cloud Services, an NVIDIA Cloud Partner in Singapore. Aperia purchased 22 servers from Dell containing NVIDIA H800 chips, which are banned in China. According to the report, Dell cut off business ties with Aperia in February 2025 due to concerns around the deal. Bloomberg found the hardware details in filings from a company called Shanghai Longteng Intelligent Computing, which was set up by Alice a decade ago. They were documented as part of the information the company had to submit to the Chinese government, since it was using its servers as a collateral for financing. While Alice hasn't been part of Shanghai Longteng since 2017 — and the documents didn't say if she was personally involved in the procurement of the chips — Huang Yu, who was identified as her sister, was the one who took over as majority owner. The filings also revealed that the company's servers included 52 units made by Super Micro Computer Inc. Those units were equipped with NVIDIA's H100 or H200 chips, which can't be sold to Chinese companies without express permission from the US government. The Shanghai AI facility where the smuggled NVIDIA units were installed is called the Yangtze River Delta Project, which Bloomberg says also has ties to Alice Huang. Its president is Kang Wei, who is being reported as Alice's husband and the person who introduced her to Jensen Huang . Alice's company Megaspeed also presented a rendering of the Yangtze River Delta Project to its investors in 2024 and claimed that it was its largest AI facility. Former NVIDIA-CEO Jensen Huang is due to testify before Congress this month , and it's likely all of this information will be pored over by officials in the run-up to the event.

sources.name: SiliconANGLE
sources.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations
sources.text: Honeypot or not, the Chinese executive/accused spy with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair this week should have been a flashing red light to him. So should fraternizing with one of your own VPs — and reportedly another employee too! In the end, all that, and maybe more to come, was just too much for Nvidia’s board to bear despite the commanding position Huang (pictured) held not only at Nvidia but in the entire artificial intelligence industry. Indeed, the speed with which he resigned — spectacularly stupid as his behavior was — still makes me wonder if there are other shoes to drop, especially on the legal or national security fronts. Market researcher SemiAnalysis thinks it came down to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community that’s very unhappy Nvidia chips have apparently been smuggled to China. Huang was something of an AI puppet master, providing the chips and software to power the entire industry as well as seemingly unlimited cash to fund and backstop everyone from AI leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic to innumerable cloud compute providers worldwide. No single person inside or outside Nvidia seems likely to fill that role. However, Nvidia really is much more than Jensen Huang. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress helped craft the financial arrangements that in part put Nvidia at the center of AI — though for what it’s worth, Huang himself wasn’t a fan lately . Some of his direct reports such as high-performance computing chief Ian Buck seem quite capable of carrying on, if perhaps not with Huang’s panache. One company is never one person, and shouldn’t be. I expect a less centralized Nvidia going forward, whoever’s at the top. More than that, AI is much more than Jensen Huang, and it will continue to be going forward. It’s easy to forget that although Huang brilliantly helped create this new wave, AI and its enablers also are what made him a rock star. But that time is now over. Nvidia and certainly the AI industry shouldn’t be depending on one person to keep everything afloat anyway. The reverberations of his sudden and shocking departure will continue to echo for a long time to come across Nvidia, its investors watching hundreds of billions of market cap evaporate, legions of Jensen fanboys and the entire artificial intelligence ecosystem. A lot of people are hoping desperately that he didn’t just pop the AI bubble (though others are hoping he did). It seems unlikely this will be the pin, but we’re dealing with a lot of unlikely things in the past week or so, for better and worse, and this shock is clearly rattling the foundations. All that managed to overshadow what otherwise would be the big news this week: Anthropic went on the road to pitch its initial public offering . It’s hoping to raise more than $64 billion and keep the AI trade humming in Nvidia’s near-term absence. Looks like next Thursday is the big day. And it’s not the only good news in AI — that is, if the IPO is successful. After a difficult month on the stock front, uber neocloud CoreWeave provided a pleasant AI surprise with upside earnings and guidance, lifting its shares almost 25% Wednesday. AI chipmaker Cerebras’ shares rose almost 18% in late trading Thursday on positive guidance and a Microsoft deal . Cisco Systems said demand is strong for AI infrastructure, even if investors shrugged, and chipmaking equipment supplier Applied Materials said AI boosted demand as well. Not everyone fared so well, though. Dutch neocloud Nebius saw its shares drop almost 17% Thursday as it lowered its outlook despite close to sevenfold revenue growth in the last quarter. The stock drop no doubt was partly because of Nvidia, which is, of course, an investor. CoreWeave –yes, another Nvidia investment — lost 7% Thursday. Couple of really big outages out there: first, Microsoft Outlook , grounding a lot of office workers, then the whole damn U.S. air traffic control system , grounding thousands of flights. Sovereignty is on many enterprise buyers’ lips these days, the notion that enterprises need a way to assert more control over their technology estates and protect their customers’ data. TheCUBE Research’s Dave Vellante and Amit Eyal Govrin just completed the first of a series of reports on how to approach sovereignty, this one focused on the hyperscale cloud providers. The software orchestrator Kubernetes has become boring, but as SiliconANGLE’s John Furrier said at this week’s KubeCon in Salt Lake City, that means it’s a success — with lessons for AI developers. “A lot of things that are happening in cloud-native that were involved in microservices in Kubernetes world are actually the same challenges in the AI world,” he noted. IBM has been working hard on quantum computing for a long time now, but at its Quantum Developer Conference in Chicago this week, it showed significant progress, according to Dave Vellante. Its goal now is to show actual industry impact by 2028, a laudable goal that presents a lot of challenges, Dave wrote in his Special Breaking Analysis this week. Next week the SC26 high-performance computing conference comes to Chicago, and theCUBE and theCUBE Research will be onsite with interviews and analysis. There’s also Microsoft Ignite in San Francisco. And earnings next week include… Nvidia! Bring the popcorn. Here’s all of this week’s enterprise and emerging tech news, most of it not salacious, along with analysis and commentary from SiliconANGLE and beyond: Breaking Analysis: Sovereign or not? Somebody give him back his Xanax! Also, I really don’t think mental illness is a compute problem. sources.name: Xataka
sources.title: Donald Trump intentó que Jensen Huang siguiera como CEO: “Nvidia es demasiado grande como para caer”
sources.text: Nvidia, la empresa que se ha convertido por méritos propios en el pegamento de la inteligencia artificial, se ha quedado sin su fundador y CEO . Estados Unidos y la propia Nvidia podían aguantar que Jensen hubiese sido víctima de una supuesta espía china , pero por políticas internas y tras conocerse otras dos relaciones extramatrimoniales con empleadas, el CEO anunció su dimisión. Ahora, el New York Times apunta que Donald Trump lleva días convenciendo a Jensen Huang para que luche por su puesto. Y tiene todo el sentido si tenemos en cuenta que Jensen, aparte del CEO de Nvidia, era una pieza geopolítica clave para el actual Gobierno estadounidense. En corto . El Times cita a dos personas relacionadas con una conversación entre Trump y Huang que se produjo en plena tormenta. El pasado martes 10 de noviembre, el presidente le pidió que siguiera luchando por su puesto de CEO. No surtió efecto porque, como decimos, una cosa era ser objeto de una supuesta trama de espionaje y otra muy distinta el incumplir normas de su compañía. A comienzos de esta semana supimos que Jensen había mantenido relaciones con la vicepresidenta de salud de Nvidia, momento en el que la junta se reunió para decidir si lo destituían o no. El asunto escaló rápido porque, horas después, el propio Jensen dimitió ... y hace apenas unas horas, Reuters informaba sobre una segunda empleada de Nvidia con la que Jensen habría tenido relaciones. Demasiado grande para caer . El motivo de la llamada y de la petición de Trump es estratégico. Estos últimos años hemos visto a ambos muy unidos, con Huang pasando de ser un "simple" CEO de una tecnológica a convertirse en una especie de mano derecha en cuestiones de Estado. Ha acompañado a otros CEO en las galas de la Casa Blanca, ha recibido medallas por parte del Gobierno y ha estado al lado de Trump en viajes clave, como el de hace unos meses a China. Nvidia es, además, una de las mayores empresas del mundo por capitalización y el puntal sobre el que Trump quiere construir esa superioridad tecnológica estadounidense. No deja de ser la que crea los chips más potentes para la IA y la que alimenta a prácticamente todas las Big Tech relacionadas con la inteligencia artificial. Según estas fuentes del Times, Trump ve el escándalo como un "simple caso de adulterio" y, también según gente de su entorno, Jensen era una especie de Henry Ford del siglo XXI gracias a que su contribución a los centros de datos podían dar un nuevo impulso industrial al país. De hecho, según estas fuentes, el motivo es uno que se ha repetido en numerosas ocasiones estos últimos meses cuando hablábamos de la industria de la IA y de todo el gasto en esta tecnología : "Nvidia es demasiado grande para caer". Aliado . La relación entre ambos en el primer mandato del presidente no fue tan estrecha, pero algo cambió cuando Trump se enteró de que Nvidia controlaba el 80% del mercado de los chips de IA avanzados. A partir de ahí, el mandamás de la tecnológica se convirtió en pieza clave para el presidente de EEUU, siendo intermediario en inversiones gigantescas en infraestructura en suelo estadounidense como en compras internacionales. Un ejemplo es el acuerdo entre Arabia Saudí y Emiratos Árabes Unidos para que compraran chips estadounidenses o, quizá, el caso más sonado: cuando Huang, tras meses de insistencia, consiguió que Trump accediera a vender tarjetas H200 a China . Hasta entonces, el Gobierno vetaba esas ventas porque no querían 'armar' al país que era (y es) el rival tecnológico y comercial, pero acordaron la venta previo arancel del 25% a los equipos como una forma de hacer que China dependa de Estados Unidos a nivel tecnológico. Al menos hasta que la tecnología de gigantes como Huawei se ponga a la par. Reconstrucción . Todo esto no deja de ser información del New York Times y, como suele ocurrir, hay que confiar en las fuentes porque todo se está desarrollando a un ritmo vertiginoso, pero tiene todo el sentido que a Trump no le interese un Huang fuera de Nvidia. De hecho, parece que las agencias estadounidenses ya sabían lo de la relación entre la supuesta espía y Huang y decidieron ocultárselo a la víctima porque Nvidia seguía siendo extremadamente útil. Ahora, toca reconstruir Nvidia , que ya tiene presidenta interina y busca sustituto para Huang. Trump ha mencionado que Tim Cook, que se acaba de jubilar en Apple, sería un candidato ideal y, de nuevo y a riesgo de quemar el meme de Xataka, tiene sentido: Cook es otra persona muy cercana al presidente, es de su confianza, estuvo hasta hace nada en la otra gran empresa del país, es alguien que ha mantenido buenas relaciones con China y con la taiwanesa TSMC. Pero claro, una cosa es lo que quiera Trump... y otra lo que termine haciendo Nvidia. Adulterio aparte, el agujero que deja Huang va a ser muy difícil de llenar. sources.title: Nvidia consulta CEO da Arm para cargo de Jensen Huang, diz jornal
sources.text: A Nvidia já tem ao menos uma pessoa em mente para o cargo de CEO após a renúncia de Jensen Huang. De acordo com o Financial Times , o nome de Rene Haas surge como candidato em potencial, embora nenhuma decisão tenha sido tomada por enquanto. O executivo é CEO da empresa britânica de semicondutores Arm , especializada em montar projetos de arquitetura de chips para outras empresas. Haas ocupa o cargo desde fevereiro de 2022. A atual empresa mais valiosa do mundo está sem gerente executivo fixo desde quinta-feira (12) , quando Huang renunciou após a divulgação de dois casos extraconjugais mantidos pelo executivo. Atualmente, a marca é comandada por uma CEO interina, Colette Kress , que também é CFO da Nvidia. Até agora, nomes externos não haviam sido considerados e até mesmo executivos da Nvidia eram pouco especulados como sucessores — Huang era um dos cofundadores da marca e ocupava de forma estável o cargo de gerência executiva desde 1993. Nvidia e Arm foram procuradas pela reportagem original, mas não se manifestaram sobre o assunto. À CNBC , a Nvidia afirmou que está “em processo de seleção de uma empresa de recrutamento para o cargo de CEO” e negou que tenha entrado “em contato com nenhum candidato em potencial” . Haas já tem familiaridade com a Nvidia por mais de um motivo. Ele trabalhou na companhia ao longo de sete anos na década de 2000 , chegando ao cargo de vice-presidente e gerente geral da divisão de computação. Em 2013, o executivo trocou a companhia pela rival Arm. Curiosamente, a trajetória de ambas as empresas quase se juntou tempos depois: em 2021, a Nvidia chegou a anunciar a aquisição da Arm por US$ 40 bilhões. Porém, a negociação foi desfeita em fevereiro do ano seguinte , após a dupla não conseguir a aprovação de órgãos reguladores. A compra recebeu pressão inclusive de fabricantes de eletrônicos, que temiam que a fusão prejudicasse a concorrência no mercado. A Arm seguiu independente e realizou a oferta pública de ações em 2023. A divisão gamer da Nvidia pode acabar? Entenda aqui o que acontecerá com a GeForce após renúncia de Jensen Huang. /Com informações de Financial Times . Why it matters: Congress smells blood in the water following bombshell reports that U.S. national security may have been jeopardized by former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese spy...

sources.name: CNBC Technology
sources.title: Nvidia scandal draws in Commerce Secretary Lutnick, who reportedly agrees to testify about China chip sales
sources.text: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee, as the fallout from ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy intensifies. Lutnick was summoned by Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott amid scrutiny over whether Nvidia could have supplied advanced artificial intelligence chips to Chinese companies and thereby potentially threatened U.S. national security. Huang and Lutnick both received letters on Thursday evening requesting them to testify in separate hearings on Dec. 3 and Dec. 10, respectively. The letter to Lutnick asked the commerce secretary to testify regarding "recent public reports about NVIDIA and the Department of Commerce's role that raises national security concerns." "Secretary Lutnick has proactively agreed to appear voluntarily before the Banking Committee to address their questions," Kristen Eichamer, a spokesperson for Lutnick, told NBC News on Thursday. CNBC contacted the Commerce Department for comment. The letter to Huang said that reports about his relationship with the alleged Chinese spy "raise significant national security concerns." Huang has acknowledged an affair with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company that has bought over $4.8 billion of advanced Nvidia AI chips over the past two years. The scandal, in addition to reports of a separate affair with a senior executive at Nvidia, led to his resignation on Thursday. There is growing bipartisan scrutiny of the Commerce Department Secretary's approach to chip policy and whether his department was doing enough to restrict the supply of AI chips to China. Lawmakers are also questioning whether the department was overseeing Nvidia's exports thoroughly enough Senator Jim Banks has been particularly scathing, saying Lutnick "appears to have used loopholes to allow some of these chip sales to occur," in an appearance on Fox News on Thursday. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass, who will chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, said on Thursday "Secretary Howard Lutnick and Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler must explain why they have not closed export control loopholes and act today to ensure our advanced technology is not fueling China's military." In a joint letter with incoming Senate Foreign Relations Chair Chris Coons published Wednesday, they said all documents relating to the export of Nvidia chips to China must be preserved. Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore. and Rep. Richard E. Neal, D-Mass. told Lutnick they were investigating the approval of sales of Nvidia chips to companies with links to the Chinese government, military and sanctioned entities. Rep. Brian Mast, R-Fla. said on Thursday that Congress needed to investigate the role of the Commerce Department in approving the export to China of AI chips, but added that he had confidence in Lutnick. Criticism is mounting on President Donald Trump 's administration for declining to include over 100 companies highlighted as national security risks on a trade blacklist, including China's AI startup DeepSeek and memory chipmaker CXMT, Reuters reported in June. Lutnick is a long-standing friend of Trump, with their relationship spanning over three decades, and is widely regarded as a close confidant of the President.

sources.title: Who is Colette Kress? Nvidia's finance chief steps in as interim CEO after Huang exit
sources.text: Nvidia Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress, a 13-year company veteran, is taking the helm of the world's most valuable chipmaker on an interim basis after Jensen Huang's sudden resignation. "She's the only one internally that has this significant respect," Dan Ives, an analyst at Yorkville Ives & Co., told CNBC before the news had been made official. "She's more than just a CFO. I'd almost view her as more of a COO." Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation Nvidia hasn't announced a succession plan and said the board is considering internal and external candidates. Kress joined Nvidia in September 2013, after holding finance roles at Cisco , Microsoft and Texas Instruments . At Nvidia, Kress has been the other big voice on earnings calls, reporting the company's results and taking questions alongside Huang. "NVIDIA's strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years," Kress said in Thursday's statement . "We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders." Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, was known for running the company with no clear second-in-command, personally deciding which projects are a priority and emailing engineers about details. But when it came to Kress, "Jensen didn't do anything without her," Ives said. "She's a Swiss Army knife for Nvidia. Anything strategically: customers, partners, technology. She was involved." CNBC spoke to nearly a dozen Nvidia insiders and former Kress co-workers. They described her as savvy, knowledgeable, thoughtful and clear-headed. Kress is stepping in at a moment of crisis. Huang has operated as Nvidia's spokesperson, the face of the company and a founder synonymous with the brand. He also pioneered the artificial intelligence chip industry, making him the central figure in the multitrillion-dollar boom that's driving the U.S. economy. Kress "deeply understands the business and has shown fierce loyalty to the company," Daniel Newman, CEO of Futurum Group, wrote in a message to CNBC. Nvidia shares plunged 14% on Thursday after the announcement. The stock is poised for its sixth straight weekly drop, the longest slump since 2012. The shares have been dragged down by broad concerns about the AI buildout, particularly after the midterm elections, which resulted in sweeping victories for Democrats. Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly results on Tuesday. The Huang saga burst into public view on Sunday, when the CEO apologized for being unfaithful to his wife. That followed reports that he'd had an affair with Alice Huang, a Chinese businesswoman whom U.S. intelligence suspects is a spy. Pressure intensified late Wednesday after The New York Times reported a second affair, this one with an employee named Kimberly Powell. Kress was recognized in May as one of Fortune's most powerful women in business. Her LinkedIn profile lists her location as Saratoga, California, a wealthy city 16 miles south of Nvidia's Santa Clara headquarters. As for the long-term leadership plan, Ives said Kress will likely serve for about a year as interim CEO but the permanent replacement will come from outside the company. "You need someone that's been on the global stage," Ives said. "Given the importance of the company not just in the U.S. tech industry but the global economy." — CNBC's Seema Mody and Jordan Novet contributed to this report

sources.title: Here's what Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones wrote to Nvidia employees
sources.text: On the heels of founder Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO of Nvidia , new interim CEO Colette Kress and board chair Harvey Jones sent emails to employees Thursday expressing gratitude and optimism for the future. CNBC obtained copies of the emails from a source familiar with the matter, who said Jones sent the first email and Kress replied shortly after. Follow CNBC's live coverage of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's resignation "The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication," Kress wrote in her email. The term Estaff is commonly used to refer to executive staff, the group of direct reports to C-suite executives at a company. Nvidia will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PST, her email said. Board chair Jones took a similar tone in his email, and praised Kress as "a key architect of NVIDIA's growth and capital strategy." "The Board has full confidence in Colette to deliver on our commitments to shareholders, customers, partners, and to each of you," Jones wrote. Below are the staff emails obtained by CNBC on Thursday. I believe deeply in this company and in its future. More than anything, I believe in each of you, in our customers and partners and in the vital role we play every day in the global economy. The Board, Estaff and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication. Thank you. This company has achieved so much because of the work that all of you bring to it every single day. You are our greatest strength. You will hear more from leadership in the coming days about our future together, and we will host a company meeting on November 18 at 9am PT. We play a vital role in building the technology that is powering the AI revolution, and we have important work ahead of us. So let's move forward together, with the same determination and commitment that have always defined this company. I am writing to share an important update. Jensen has resigned as CEO and Board Member, and the Board has asked our Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress to serve as interim CEO while it conducts a search for a permanent successor looking at both internal and external candidates. I will serve as the first-ever Chair of the Board. As CFO for over 13 years, Colette has been a key architect of NVIDIA's growth and capital strategy. She possesses a deep understanding of this business and the markets in which we operate. The Board has full confidence in Colette to deliver on our commitments to shareholders, customers, partners, and to each of you. Jensen's contributions to NVIDIA are profound. NVIDIA is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. We pioneered accelerated computing, defined the modern GPU, and built the platform that powered artificial intelligence. The Board takes seriously our duty as stewards of this great company. The strength of this company resides in our employees, leadership team, technical strength and partner ecosystem. I am confident that under Colette's leadership, with the full support of the Board, we will continue to grow our business, and lead the industry forward. Thank you for your focus, your professionalism, and your commitment to NVIDIA. Harvey Jones Chair, NVIDIA Board of Directors

sources.title: Who is Colette Kress, NVIDIA's interim CEO?
sources.text: Kress spent 25 years in various finance roles before joining NVIDIA in 2013 After 33 years as the chief executive officer of NVIDIA, Jensen Huang has resigned from the AI and gaming giant he founded . On Thursday morning, the company's board of director announced Colette Kress , NVIDIA's current executive vice president and chief financial officer, as Huang's temporary replacement. "The Board has full confidence in Colette and the leadership team, and we expect the company's operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption," newly-minted NVIDIA board chair Harvey Jones said in a release announcing Thursday's news. Kress is a relative unknown, but is taking lead of NVIDIA at tumultuous time in the company's history. Huang departure comes days after NVIDIA's board said it would investigate Huang after he admitted to having an affair with a former tech executive accused of being a Chinese intelligence asset. The New York Times later reported that Huang had also had an affair with an NVIDIA executive who reported to him. Before the revelations, the company did not have a succession plan in place. And for at least the immediate future, it's now on Kress to lead the company. Here's what we know about the executive. Kress worked at three companies before joining NVIDIA. She first spent eight years in finance roles at Texas Instruments before joining Microsoft in 1997. In 2006, six years after Steve Ballmer took over as Microsoft's CEO, she became the chief financial officer of the company's Server and Tools division. She remained with the company until 2010, when she moved to Cisco. There, she was the senior vice president and chief financial officer of the company's Business Technology and Operations Finance unit. To hear Kress tell it, Huang went out of his way to recruit her. Sometime before she joined NVIDIA in 2013, the CEO apparently sketched his vision for the company on a whiteboard. Per a 2023 interview , Huang wanted to transform NVIDIA into the dominant player in the nascent AI industry. Say what you will about Huang's personal life and judgement, the man was an AI visionary. It would be almost another four years following Kress joining NVIDIA before a group of Google researchers published " Attention Is All You Need ," the paper that introduced the world to transformer models, and nearly a decade before the release of ChatGPT. Kress partly credits her sons, who were only eight and 10 at the time, for buying Huang's pitch. Despite their young age, the two already knew of NVIDIA and its importance to gaming. In a 2024 Fortune interview , Kress said NVIDIA was the smallest company she had worked for when she joined in 2013. At the start of her tenure, NVIDIA's revenue was $4.28 billion for the year . In fiscal 2026, the company recorded a record $215.9 billion in revenue. When NVIDIA's board of directors announced Kress as Huang's temporary successor, it said it would consider both internal and external candidates to take on the role of CEO permanently, leaving the door open for her and other current NVIDIA employees to win the job. In any case, it's far too early to speculate who the company's board might interview for the job. But if you can forgive a writer a tired analogy, if Kress stays on as CEO, she is likely to be a Tim Cook-like figure, one that can stabilize the company and guide it toward continued growth. "The Board, [executive staff] and I recognize that this has been an extraordinarily difficult period and I want you to know how grateful we are for your resilience, professionalism and continued dedication," Kress wrote in her first email to NVIDIA employees after the transition was announced, according to CNBC . Still, she has a very difficult job ahead of her. Huang has agreed to testify before Congress in a hearing that the House aims to hold before the Thanksgiving holiday. The chair of the House Foreign Affairs committee, Brian Mast of Florida, said he wasn't ruling out the possibility of "public hearings for other people or other things down road." You can bet NVIDIA is likely to face an intense amount of scrutiny in the coming weeks, particularly when Democrats take control of the House and Senate at the start of next year.

sources.title: Google’s latest Search upgrade promises better answers to your most complicated questions
sources.text: Google Search is getting better at understanding complicated questions, including those with multiple parts, highly specific requests, or confusing typos. The updates are coming via the company’s newly released Gemini 4 Hydrogen model, which Google claims is its “biggest model improvement to Search yet.” While Google’s frontier models, Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, are best at deep reasoning for hard problems, Hydrogen is designed for fast execution across a variety of agentic workflows, or tasks in which an AI carries out multiple steps on its own, the company explained in an announcement. The idea behind the model’s release is that using the most powerful model isn’t always needed — sometimes a faster, cheaper, and reasonably smart one will do. Google says Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash, its previous fast model, but it’s still pretty smart, even beating the more powerful Gemini 4 Argon on one broad intelligence benchmark, the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index , at its default high thinking level. In Search, Hydrogen brings several improvements, including a better understanding of user intent, the ability to offer more helpful links and visual responses, and better answers across the different languages supported by Google’s AI Mode. In terms of intent, Google says Hydrogen can handle more nuanced and complicated questions more quickly. This means people can ask their questions in their natural train of thought, including those that have multiple parts or that include highly specific requests. Hydrogen is also better at navigating hard-to-understand typos, Google says. Because of its improvements and better ability to follow instructions and call the right tools, Hydrogen is able to more precisely address each part of a user’s question. Its advanced reasoning also improves Search’s fan-out technique, which breaks down a single user’s prompt into multiple subqueries. This allows people to discover websites related to the query that they may have otherwise missed, the blog post explains. The addition of Hydrogen to Search will also mean more images, structured responses, comparison tables, and custom tools will appear as visual responses to users’ queries in AI Mode. Google also says Hydrogen can work on its own for everyday work in areas like writing code, running tests, or verifying code changes, or it can be paired with Carbon and Argon in workflows that combine several models. The model offers four thinking levels: low, medium, high (default), and a new, extra-high tier (“xhigh”), all of which are designed to complete tasks faster with fewer output tokens. On multi-step tasks like deep research, data analysis, and broad codebase navigation, Hydrogen ranks No. 5 on Agent Arena’s benchmarks, the company pointed out. In addition to Search, Gemini 4 Hydrogen is coming to all tiers of Google’s AI Studio, the Gemini API, the Gemini App, and the paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers in Google’s Antigravity development platform. Google says the Hydrogen update is rolling out to all Search users globally. When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission . sources.title: Google’s new Gemini model is better at understanding complicated questions
sources.text: Google’s Robby Stein says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is ‘the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.’﻿ Google’s Robby Stein says Gemini 4 Hydrogen is ‘the biggest model upgrade to Search yet.’﻿ Google says its new Gemini 4 Hydrogen model can give more helpful answers to complex questions, including “questions with multiple parts, hard-to-understand typos, or highly specific requests.” The new model can break down your questions and address each part in its responses. It’s available starting today in search, the Gemini app, all tiers of Google AI Studio, the Gemini API, Gemini for business, and in Google Antigravity for Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers. Robby Stein, VP of product at Google Search, says it’s “now the new default model in AI Mode & being used for your hardest questions in AI Overviews.” Google says Gemini 4 Hydrogen also gives users a wider range of links in its responses by “conducting simultaneous queries across all the relevant subtopics.” Its responses have more visuals, too, like images, comparison tables, graphs, and maps. One of Stein’s examples shows the AI generating an interactive animated driving simulation in response to a user’s question about how phones locate which lane of a highway a car is on in areas without cell service. Google says the new model also has improved language understanding “across all supported AI Mode languages.” Users have more thinking level options with Gemini 4 Hydrogen, as well, including low, medium, high, and a new “xhigh” mode. According to Google, the new model “delivers significant leaps in both speed and intelligence” compared to Gemini Flash 3.8 , and it “matches or outperforms some of the competing models in its class,” like Claude Sonnet 5.5 and GPT-6.1 Terra.

stories.summary: The AI boom without Jensen Huang will test a hard truth: Even if the tech world has grown somewhat less reliant on Nvidia's chips, it remains highly dependent on its checkbook. Why it matters : With rival chips maturing and recent software breakthroughs, the tech ecosystem has achieved what would've seemed impossible a year ago: a viable path around Nvidia.
